:::{#exm-breusch-pagan-bw}
#### Breusch--Pagan test for the `birthweight` interaction model

For the `birthweight` interaction model (@eq-BW-lm-interact),
$z_i$ holds sex, gestational age, and their interaction,
so $q = 3$.
We fit both auxiliary regressions by hand
and compare the results with `lmtest::bptest()`:

```{r}
bp_data <-
  bw |>
  mutate(
    resid_sq = resid(bw_lm2)^2,
    g = resid_sq / mean(resid_sq)
  )

bp_n <- nobs(bw_lm2)

bp_aux <- lm(resid_sq ~ sex + age + sex:age, data = bp_data)
bp_r2 <- summary(bp_aux)$r.squared
bp_stat <- bp_n * bp_r2
bp_p <- pchisq(bp_stat, df = 3, lower.tail = FALSE)

bp_aux_g <- lm(g ~ sex + age + sex:age, data = bp_data)
bp_ess <- sum((fitted(bp_aux_g) - mean(bp_data$g))^2)
bp_orig <- bp_ess / 2
bp_orig_p <- pchisq(bp_orig, df = 3, lower.tail = FALSE)

lmtest::bptest(bw_lm2)
lmtest::bptest(bw_lm2, studentize = FALSE)
```

By @def-breusch-pagan,
the studentized statistic is:

$$
\ba
\text{BP}
&\eqdef n R^2_{\text{aux}}
&& \text{(definition of the studentized statistic)}
\\
&= `r bp_n` \times `r round(bp_r2, 5)`
&& \text{(substitute } n \text{ and } R^2_{\text{aux}}\text{)}
\\
&\approx `r round(bp_stat, 3)`
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-breusch-pagan-bw-studentized}

and the original statistic is:

$$
\ba
\text{BP}_{\text{orig}}
&\eqdef \tfrac{1}{2} \text{ESS}_g
&& \text{(definition of the original statistic)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \times `r round(bp_ess, 4)`
&& \text{(substitute the explained sum of squares)}
\\
&\approx `r round(bp_orig, 3)`
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-breusch-pagan-bw-original}

Comparing each value with a $\chi^2_3$ distribution
(@thm-breusch-pagan-null)
gives $p \approx `r round(bp_p, 2)`$
for the studentized statistic
and $p \approx `r round(bp_orig_p, 2)`$
for the original statistic,
which match `bptest()`.
Neither test gives evidence
that the error variance changes with sex or gestational age.
The two statistics differ noticeably.
The original statistic divides the explained sum of squares by 2,
the variance that $g_i$ would have if the errors were Gaussian;
the studentized statistic equals the same explained sum of squares
divided by the mean squared deviation of the $g_i$ values
(their variance with divisor $n$) instead,
which here is about
`r round(mean((bp_data$g - mean(bp_data$g))^2), 2)`.
A non-significant result from only `r bp_n` babies
is weak evidence that the variance is constant,
so we would still look at the residual plots.
:::
